What are Empirical dissertations?

An empirical dissertation is a type of research-based academic writing that involves data collection and analysis to test a hypothesis or answer a research question. This type of dissertation is based on collecting primary data through surveys, experiments, or observations. Empirical dissertations typically follow a structured research methodology, which includes designing research questions, selecting participants or subjects, collecting data, analysing data using statistical methods, and drawing conclusions based on the data analysis. Empirical dissertations are common in fields such as psychology, sociology, and economics. Data collection and analysis are critical to answering research questions and advancing the understanding of a specific phenomenon.
